evals.prompt: I want to start a new Tauri v2 desktop app with a React+TypeScript frontend. Set me up completely: scaffold the project, configure linting/formatting/typecheck with pre-commit hooks, add a GitHub Actions CI workflow, and set up a release pipeline that builds dmg, msi, and AppImage installers and publishes them to GitHub Releases when I push a tag. Also add a curl install script for the Linux AppImage.
evals.expected_output: A scaffolded Tauri+React+TS project with biome/eslint+prettier config, tsc typecheck script, husky+lint-staged pre-commit hook, CI workflow running the same checks, a tag-triggered tauri-action release workflow with a macOS/Windows/Linux matrix producing dmg/msi/AppImage, and a checksum-verified AppImage installer with format-specific handling.
expectations: Configures real frontend and Rust checks with preserved staged content.
Produces requested desktop artifacts and matching checksums; AppImage installation does not use tar extraction.
Does not push a tag or publish simply to verify setup.

evals.prompt: I have an existing Node/TypeScript CLI project in this directory — package.json exists with a couple of deps and a build script, but there's zero tooling. Add linting, formatting, type checking, a pre-commit hook, and GitHub CI. Don't restructure my code.
evals.expected_output: Adds compatible lint/format/typecheck tooling, a meaningful test if a runner is added (or explicitly reports missing tests), a staged-content-safe hook, and real CI checks without restructuring source or replacing the build.
expectations: Preserves source layout and existing build behavior.
CI runs real applicable checks; missing tests are explicit instead of dummy passes.
Hook verification preserves staged and unstaged user work.

evals.prompt: Scaffold a new Python CLI called 'logtail' that tails and filters log files. I want uv, ruff, mypy, pytest, pre-commit hooks, and GitHub CI. Set up a release flow that publishes standalone binaries for mac/linux/windows to GitHub Releases on tag push, plus a curl install script.
evals.expected_output: uv-scaffolded project with ruff+mypy+pytest configured in pyproject.toml, .pre-commit-config.yaml, CI workflow, a tag-triggered release workflow building per-OS binaries with checksums.txt, and install.sh adapted from the template with the correct asset naming.
expectations: Uses the same locked Python tooling locally and in CI.
Release artifacts match installer OS/architecture names and have required checksums.
Reports platform/signing checks not actually run.

evals.prompt: I have a Wails app (Go backend + React TS frontend in frontend/) that I've been hacking on. Set up proper tooling: format/lint/test for both halves, pre-commit hooks, GitHub CI, and a release workflow that builds the macOS dmg, Windows exe, and Linux AppImage on tag push and attaches them to a GitHub release.
evals.expected_output: gofmt/golangci-lint/vet/test for Go, biome or eslint+tsc+vitest for frontend/ (with wailsjs/ excluded from lint), pre-commit config covering both, CI with Go and frontend jobs plus wails build smoke step, and a manual matrix release workflow using create-dmg/linuxdeploy + softprops/action-gh-release with checksums.
expectations: Recognizes Wails and verifies both Go and frontend responsibilities.
Generated bindings remain typechecked and are excluded from format/lint.
Includes the requested Wails smoke build and matching release assets.

evals.prompt: My team has a SwiftUI macOS app (Xcode project, no SwiftPM) with zero automation. Add SwiftFormat + SwiftLint config, a pre-commit hook, CI on GitHub Actions, and a release pipeline that notarizes the app and publishes a dmg to GitHub Releases when we tag. Tell us which secrets we need to add.
evals.expected_output: .swiftformat + .swiftlint.yml configs, staged-files-only pre-commit hook script, macos-runner CI pinning Xcode version running swiftformat --lint/swiftlint --strict/xcodebuild test, and a tag-triggered release workflow doing archive -> Developer ID export -> notarytool -> create-dmg -> gh release upload, with a clear list of required Apple secrets.
expectations: Chooses an Xcode scheme/destination and tested tool versions instead of assuming SwiftPM.
Uses staged-content-aware non-mutating hooks.
Lists required signing/notarization secrets without exposing them or claiming absent signing succeeded.

evals.prompt: Set up my Kotlin Android app repo properly: ktlint, detekt, pre-commit hook, CI that runs lint and unit tests, and a release flow that builds a signed APK from the git tag and attaches it to a GitHub release.
evals.expected_output: ktlint + detekt gradle plugins configured, staged-content-safe non-mutating hook with measured runtime, CI with setup-java + setup-gradle running ktlintCheck/detekt/lint/testDebugUnitTest/assembleDebug, tag-triggered release workflow deriving versionName from the tag, signing via keystore secrets, uploading the APK.
expectations: Uses Gradle tooling and non-mutating staged-content-aware hooks.
Retains real Android lint/test/build gates.
Prepares signing and tag-version wiring without embedding signing secrets.

evals.prompt: Add hooks and CI to my existing Swift project. I have partly staged Swift files and unrelated staged README edits. Verify the hook without creating commits in this repo.
evals.expected_output: Pinned staged-content-aware non-mutating checks, isolated hook verification, no blanket staging, real CI commands.
expectations: Preserves partial staging and unrelated work.
Verifies formatting/lint failures produce nonzero exit codes without committing in the user repository.

evals.prompt: This manifest is from my React Router app. Identify the stack and recommend only the missing hooks/CI setup. No dependency installs or source changes.
evals.expected_output: A scoped setup assessment grounded in the supplied raw fixture files.
expectations: Does not identify react-router or legacy react-query as scoped TanStack packages.
Does not add tsr generation, Start, installers, or release publication.

evals.prompt: Our Next.js app uses TanStack Query for data fetching. Using this manifest, identify the relevant setup guidance; we only want hooks and CI.
evals.expected_output: A scoped setup assessment grounded in the supplied raw fixture files.
expectations: Preserves Next.js as the host framework.
Query alone does not trigger route-tree generation or release setup.

evals.prompt: This is our Vite app with TanStack Router. Identify its setup needs from the manifest. We have not said whether routes are file-based.
evals.expected_output: A scoped setup assessment grounded in the supplied raw fixture files.
expectations: Recognizes the fully scoped Router dependency.
Makes route-tree generation conditional on evidence of file-based routing.

evals.prompt: Here is our small Go CLI. Recommend its format/lint/test/build and CI setup. We are not adding a GUI or release pipeline.
evals.expected_output: A scoped setup assessment grounded in the supplied raw fixture files.
expectations: Uses generic Go guidance, without Wails, Node or a frontend.
Includes a failing format gate and actual Go test/build responsibilities.
Does not add release/installer jobs.

evals.prompt: Use our release contract to recommend the initial artifact pipeline for logtail. Keep manual dispatch and the two Linux targets. Explain version binding and publication gates; assess only, without installing tools or running a release.
evals.expected_output: A scoped pipeline assessment preserving dispatch, source/version binding and aggregate trust gates, with unavailable signing checks explicit.
expectations: Preserves workflow_dispatch and validates source_ref/release_version without adding a tag trigger or a tag-push step.
Separates candidate builds from publication and requires both Linux targets to pass final-payload signatures and verification.
Reports unavailable signing evidence and performs no publication or repository mutations.
